properties.name: urn:ogc:def:crs:OGC:1.3:CRS84
Long Wharf, inner part (SF&O ferry wharf 1863; filled 1879-82 into the Oakland Mole)
properties.note: Gibbons' wharf (1852) used as the San Francisco & Oakland Railroad ferry landing; SF&O trains from Sept 1863; Central Pacific acquired and extended it from 1868; reconstructed by landfill 1879-80, Oakland Pier opened on the fill 1882-01-22. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1899 sheet (the mole line).

properties.name: Long Wharf, outer trestle to deep water (freight only after 1882)
properties.note: Transcontinental terminus from 1869-11-08; reached deep water (11,000 ft) and fully open 1871-01-16; freight-only after 1882; abandoned 1919. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1899 sheet.

properties.name: Oakland Mole (fill) and train shed
properties.note: Built on the filled Long Wharf 1879-82, opened 1882-01-22; SP main-line and East Bay local trains (electric 1911-1939); last SP ferry 1958-07-29; demolished in the 1960s for the Port of Oakland. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1899 sheet.

properties.name: Western Pacific Mole on the north training wall of the estuary
properties.note: Built 1906-10 along the north jetty of the Oakland Harbor entrance; WP ferry terminal opened 1910 (passenger service from Aug 1910), used until 1933, passenger terminal demolished 1940. Dates of the month ESTIMATED. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1915 sheet.

properties.name: Key System Mole: causeway (trestle 1903, filled 1908-16) to the ferry pier
properties.note: Transbay service from 1903-10-26 on a 17,000 ft wooden trestle; approach filled 1908, causeway except the last 3,800 ft by 1916; pier fire 1933-05-06 (rebuilt slightly to the south); ferries to the Bay Bridge 1939-01-15, Exposition trains/ferries until 1939-10-29. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1915 sheet ('San Francisco-Oakland Terminal Key Route Pier').

properties.name: Alameda Terminal wharf at the foot of Pacific Ave
properties.note: SF&A ferry wharf (~3,750 ft) built 1864, first run 1864-08-25; transcontinental terminus 1869-09-06 to 1869-11-07; abandoned for rail-ferry use 1873 (wharf later used by the Pacific Coast Oil refinery). Geometry: the wharf on the USGS San Francisco 1899 sheet.

properties.name: Pacific Ave, private right-of-way to 5th St
properties.note: 'Along Pacific Avenue to 4th Street, then via private right-of-way to 5th Street' (SF&A); unused after the wharf closed in 1873 (end ESTIMATED). Private right-of-way approximate.

properties.name: Lincoln Ave (Linnet St / Railroad Ave): 5th St - Park St - Fernside
properties.note: SF&A 1864 (Alameda station at Park St); Central Pacific 1869-70, SP; electrified 1911 (Lincoln Avenue line, to the Alameda Mole from 1906); passenger service ended January 1941, freight 1960 when the rails were removed. Geometry: today's Lincoln Avenue centreline (OSM).

properties.name: Park St - Fernside - Melrose (across the neck cut by the Tidal Canal in 1903)
properties.note: SF&A main line to San Leandro and Haywards (1865); after 1873 Alameda trains ran north from Fernside to Fruitvale and this link carried freight; still on the 1915 map; end ESTIMATED with the Lincoln Ave freight (1960). Geometry: USGS Concord 1897 sheet.

properties.name: Melrose - Fitchburg - Elmhurst - San Leandro (later the CP/SP main line, now UP Niles Sub)
properties.note: SF&A route of 1865 'through Fernside, Melrose, Fitchburg and Elmhurst' to San Leandro; part of the Central Pacific main line from 1869; today's Union Pacific Niles Subdivision (geometry: OSM).

properties.name: San Leandro - Haywards on Ward St and the county road (East 14th St / Mission Blvd)
properties.note: Street running 'along Ward Street in San Leandro and the county road (now East 14th Street/Mission Boulevard) to Watkins Street, Hayward' (1865); abandoned 1873. Geometry: today's East 14th St / Mission Blvd (OSM); the San Leandro end is approximate.

properties.name: Alameda Mole: stone mole and ferry pier (2.5 mi to deep water)
properties.note: SPC extended its West End wharf ~2.5 miles NW on a stone mole, terminal opened 1884-03-15 (Alameda Post); dual gauge 1898, standard gauge after 1906; terminal burned 1902-11-20 and was rebuilt larger and farther out; SP electric trains 1911-1939; ferries ended 1939-01-15; the Navy demolished the terminal in 1940 for NAS Alameda. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1915 sheet ('Southern Pacific' on the south jetty).

properties.name: West End wharves (first SPC ferry terminal)
properties.note: A pair of 1,000 ft wharves at the old shoreline where Main Street bends west; ferries Bay City and Garden City to San Francisco; replaced by the mole (1884). Wikipedia dates the Alameda ferry terminal to 1878-03-20, the Alameda Post the wharves to summer 1879. Wharf outline APPROXIMATE.

properties.name: Main Street across the marsh (West End)
properties.note: 'Along Main [Street] over the marshland to the wharves'; electric (Encinal Avenue line) 1911; last train January 1941. Geometry: USGS San Francisco 1899 sheet + today's Main Street.
properties.geometry_source: topo sf1899 (99% on ink); road (snap 8 m, dev 19 m)

properties.name: Central Ave (trestle along the shore from Main St to 4th St) and Encinal Ave to High St
properties.note: Test train on Encinal Ave 1877-12-02; service Park St - Los Gatos 1878-03-20; trestle on Central Ave over the water 4th St - Main St; 33 trains a day by 1888; standard gauge from 1906; SP electric Encinal Avenue line from 1911-06-01; last service 1941-01-18. Geometry: today's Central and Encinal Avenue centrelines (OSM).
properties.geometry_source: road (snap 13 m, dev 88 m); road (snap 6 m, dev 26 m)

properties.name: Encinal Ave east of High St to Fernside (bridge abutment)
properties.note: Approach to the San Leandro Bay swing bridge; unused after the bridge was abandoned (1906).

properties.name: Swing bridge across San Leandro Bay
properties.note: Bay and Coast Railroad (SPC) swing bridge from Fernside/Encinal across San Leandro Bay; damaged in the 1906 earthquake and abandoned (Alameda track isolated). Geometry: USGS Haywards 1899 sheet; the west abutment at today's Encinal Ave / Fernside Blvd (Alameda Post).

properties.name: Trestle across the San Leandro Bay marsh to West San Leandro
properties.note: Trestles and fill of the Bay and Coast Railroad (1878) across the marsh; abandoned with the bridge after the 1906 earthquake. Geometry: USGS Haywards 1899 sheet ('Southern [Pacific]').

properties.name: West San Leandro - West San Lorenzo - Mt Eden - Alvarado - Newark (Bay and Coast RR)
properties.note: Bay and Coast Railroad trestles and fill from Newark to Alameda (1878); standard gauge 1906-09; SP Coast line, now the Union Pacific Coast Subdivision (geometry: OSM). The 1906 link north to the SP main at Elmhurst is a separate segment.

properties.name: Elmhurst connection to the SP main line (after the 1906 earthquake)
properties.note: Built when the San Leandro Bay bridge was abandoned (date ESTIMATED); today's UP Coast Subdivision junction (geometry: OSM).

properties.name: Newark - Alviso (Drawbridge) - Agnew - Santa Clara
properties.note: Santa Clara Valley RR / SPC narrow gauge from Dumbarton Point and Newark to San Jose, completed 1876 (month ESTIMATED); standard gauge 1906-09; now UP Coast Subdivision (geometry: OSM).

properties.name: Newark - Dumbarton Point
properties.note: The SPC's first ferry terminal at Dumbarton Point (1876), used until the line to Alameda opened (1878); end ESTIMATED. The 1910 Dumbarton Cutoff runs on the same corridor; geometry follows it (LOW CONFIDENCE).

properties.name: Oakland Point - 1st St (Embarcadero) - Brooklyn - Fruitvale - Melrose
properties.note: Transcontinental trains to the Oakland Long Wharf from 1869-11-08 (via the SF&O 7th St line); the First Street line was completed 1870 (SF&A article). SP main, now UP Niles Subdivision (geometry: OSM).

properties.name: San Leandro - Haywards - Decoto - Niles
properties.note: Western Pacific (1862) / Central Pacific line from Niles to San Leandro; first through train reached the Alameda wharf 1869-09-06 over a temporary connection to the SF&A at San Leandro. Today's UP Niles Subdivision (geometry: OSM).

properties.name: San Francisco: 12th & Mission - 12th St - Division (trestle over the SP) - Florida - Mariposa - Potrero Ave - Army St - Old San Bruno Rd (electric street section)
properties.note: Depot at the SE corner of 12th & Mission; electrified 600 V (city franchise) to the Army St shops; street sections from DataSF intersections (route per the earlier routes.csv research). North-end service from 1907-10-02; mainline service ended 1920-07-31 (a southeast-SF piece later carried Western Pacific freight into the 1980s - which piece is not documented here).

properties.name: San Francisco: Islais Creek / Alemany grade to Daly City
properties.note: 'then steam via Barneveld/Loomis and the Alemany Blvd (Islais Creek) grade'; the OSR's Mission (5.4 mi) and Daly City (7.6 mi) stations fit this alignment; geometry follows today's Alemany Boulevard (built on the grade; OSM).

properties.name: Daly City - Crosby - Thornton - Mussel Rock - Edgemar - Salada - Brighton - Vallemar - Rockaway
properties.note: Along the face of the sea cliffs from Thornton to Mussel Rock (the San Andreas rift crossing), then the beach terraces of Salada (Sharp Park) and Rockaway. Geometry: USGS San Mateo 1915 sheet ('Ocean Shore').

properties.name: Rockaway - Pedro Valley (Tobin)
properties.note: Tobin station at San Pedro Point (Danmann Ave / Shelter Cove Rd), reached 1907-10-02. Geometry hand-placed along the valley floor (LOW CONFIDENCE).

properties.name: Tobin - Shelter Cove (San Pedro Point)
properties.note: Along today's Shelter Cove road (on the grade); extension south opened to Granada June 1908.

properties.name: Pedro Point tunnel
properties.note: Tunnel through San Pedro Point (built during construction, 1905-08). Position APPROXIMATE.

properties.name: Cliff shelf round Devil's Slide to Montara
properties.note: Shelf cut into the sea cliffs of Montara Mountain round Devil's Slide; washed out January 1916 and the track relocated round the slide. Hand-placed along the cliff and the 1937 highway (USGS Montara Mountain 1949 sheet) - LOW CONFIDENCE.

properties.name: Montara - Farallone - Moss Beach
properties.note: Montara station (222 Second St) and Farallone City (Seventh St); the grade is under today's Cabrillo Highway in Montara (OSM abandoned:railway, old operator Ocean Shore Railway); Moss Beach approximate.

properties.name: Moss Beach - Princeton - North Granada - Granada
properties.note: Granada reached June 1908; North Granada depot (1900 building) at 10151 Cabrillo Hwy. Geometry hand-placed along the shore of Half Moon Bay (LOW CONFIDENCE).

properties.name: Granada - Miramar - Half Moon Bay
properties.note: 'Ocean Shore' station reached October 1908 (Half Moon Bay; Arleta Park depot at 920 Railroad Ave). Geometry: OSM grade fragments (Miramar, Half Moon Bay), hand-placed between.
properties.geometry_source: rail (snap 6 m, dev 60 m); pts; rail (snap 8 m, dev 14 m)

properties.name: Half Moon Bay - Arleta - Purisima - Lobitos - Tunitas Glen
properties.note: End of track at Tunitas Glen (1908, month ESTIMATED); a Stanley Steamer auto stage bridged the 26-mile gap to Swanton. Geometry: OSM grade fragments south of Half Moon Bay and at Purisima, hand-placed between (south of Purisima LOW CONFIDENCE).
properties.geometry_source: pts; rail (snap 6 m, dev 4 m); pts; rail (snap 5 m, dev 57 m); pts
